_about: The literature behind grand-questions.json, keyed so each grand question can cite without repeating bibliographic detail. Every record here was FETCHED: 36 from the Europe PMC REST API, 14 by direct Crossref DOI lookup, several cross-checked in both. `quotable` is text actually seen in the fetched record (title or abstract), so a reader can tell the record was opened rather than recalled. Records with no abstract in the index say so in `note` and quote the title.
scope: Verification here means the bibliographic record exists with the stated title, year and venue. It does NOT mean the full text was read, that the paper's conclusions are endorsed, or that the selection is representative of its field: for the disputed questions two or three papers are named per side, which is a pointer to a dispute and not a review of it. Six entries are books or lectures (Fisher 1930, Thompson 1917, Maynard Smith & Szathmary 1995, Okasha 2006, Medawar 1952) verified through Crossref monograph or reprint DOIs rather than as indexed articles; `is_book` marks them and their details should be checked against a physical copy before quoting. Nothing avian is cited: one bird-adjacent candidate was replaced with a mammal-only paper, because this project holds a clade out as a blind exam.

boyle2017.ref: Boyle EA, Li YI, Pritchard JK (2017). An Expanded View of Complex Traits: From Polygenic to Omnigenic. Cell 169:1177-1186.
boyle2017.quotable: A central goal of genetics is to understand the links between genetic variation and disease
boyle2017.note: foundational statement of the omnigenic model

manolio2009.ref: Manolio TA, Collins FS, Cox NJ, Goldstein DB, Hindorff LA, Hunter DJ, McCarthy MI, et al. (2009). Finding the missing heritability of complex diseases. Nature 461:747-753.
manolio2009.quotable: Genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of genetic variants associated with complex human diseases and traits

wagner2011pleiotropy.ref: Wagner GP, Zhang J (2011). The pleiotropic structure of the genotype-phenotype map: the evolvability of complex organisms. Nature Reviews Genetics 12:204-213.
wagner2011pleiotropy.quotable: Because pleiotropy was found so frequently, the notion arose that pleiotropy is 'universal'
wagner2011pleiotropy.note: structural account of why the genotype-phenotype map is hard

wolpert1969.ref: Wolpert L (1969). Positional information and the spatial pattern of cellular differentiation. Journal of Theoretical Biology 25:1-47.
wolpert1969.quotable: Positional information and the spatial pattern of cellular differentiation
wolpert1969.note: FOUNDATIONAL, the French Flag paper. The Europe PMC record carries no abstract, so the quotable line is the title.

turing1952.ref: Turing AM (1952). The chemical basis of morphogenesis. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London B 237:37-72.
turing1952.note: FOUNDATIONAL, verified by direct DOI lookup; Crossref returns metadata only. Europe PMC indexes only the 1990 Bull Math Biol reprint (PMID 2185858).

gregor2007.ref: Gregor T, Tank DW, Wieschaus EF, Bialek W (2007). Probing the limits to positional information. Cell 130:153-164.
gregor2007.quotable: The reproducibility and precision of biological patterning is limited by the accuracy with which concentration profiles of morphogen molecules can be established

jaeger2020.ref: Jaeger J, Verd B (2020). Dynamic positional information: Patterning mechanism versus precision in gradient-driven systems. Current Topics in Developmental Biology 137:219-246.
jaeger2020.quotable: There is much talk about information in biology
jaeger2020.note: critique of the static positional-information framing

szathmary1995nature.ref: Szathmary E, Maynard Smith J (1995). The major evolutionary transitions. Nature 374:227-232.
szathmary1995nature.note: FOUNDATIONAL journal statement; verified by direct DOI lookup, metadata only.

maynardsmith1995book.ref: Maynard Smith J, Szathmary E (1995). The Major Transitions in Evolution. Oxford University Press.
maynardsmith1995book.note: FOUNDATIONAL. A BOOK, not an indexed article. Crossref carries it as an OUP monograph with issued year 1997 (the Oxford paperback reissue); the first edition is 1995.

szathmary2015.ref: Szathmary E (2015). Toward major evolutionary transitions theory 2.0. PNAS 112:10104-10111.
szathmary2015.quotable: The impressive body of work on the major evolutionary transitions in the last 20 y calls for a reconstruction of the theory

price1970.ref: Price GR (1970). Selection and covariance. Nature 227:520-521.
price1970.note: FOUNDATIONAL, the Price equation. Crossref metadata only; Crossref renders the title with initial capitals.

price1972ext.ref: Price GR (1972). Extension of covariance selection mathematics. Annals of Human Genetics 35:485-490.
price1972ext.note: the multilevel extension. The DOI genuinely carries a legacy '1957' string; confirmed independently by direct Crossref lookup, which returns year 1972, Annals of Human Genetics 35:485-490. No abstract in the record.

frank2012price.ref: Frank SA (2012). Natural selection. IV. The Price equation. Journal of Evolutionary Biology 25:1002-1019.
frank2012price.quotable: The Price equation partitions total evolutionary change into two components

okasha2006.ref: Okasha S (2006). Evolution and the Levels of Selection. Oxford University Press.
okasha2006.quotable: Evolution and the Levels of Selection
okasha2006.note: A BOOK (Crossref type: monograph). Chapter listing confirmed, e.g. 'Selection at Multiple Levels: Concepts and Methods', pp 40-75.

hamilton1964.ref: Hamilton WD (1964). The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I. Journal of Theoretical Biology 7:1-16.
hamilton1964.quotable: The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I.
hamilton1964.note: FOUNDATIONAL, Hamilton's rule. Part II also verified: PMID 5875340, DOI 10.1016/0022-5193(64)90039-6. No abstract in the record.

nowak2010.ref: Nowak MA, Tarnita CE, Wilson EO (2010). The evolution of eusociality. Nature 466:1057-1062.
nowak2010.quotable: Eusociality, in which some individuals reduce their own lifetime reproductive potential to raise the offspring of others
nowak2010.side: against the generality and usefulness of inclusive-fitness theory

abbot2011.ref: Abbot P, Abe J, Alcock J, Alizon S, Alpedrinha JA, Andersson M, et al. (2011). Inclusive fitness theory and eusociality. Nature 471:E1-E4.
abbot2011.quotable: Nowak et al. argue that inclusive fitness theory has been of little value in explaining the natural world
abbot2011.side: for inclusive-fitness theory; the multi-author reply
abbot2011.note: the record's page field reads 'E1-4; author reply E9-10'

gardner2011.ref: Gardner A, West SA, Wild G (2011). The genetical theory of kin selection. Journal of Evolutionary Biology 24:1020-1043.
gardner2011.quotable: Natural selection operates both directly, via the impact of a trait upon the individual's own fitness, and indirectly
gardner2011.side: for the generality of Hamilton's rule, formally argued

birch2014.ref: Birch J (2014). Hamilton's Rule and Its Discontents. The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science 65:381-411.
birch2014.side: separates the formal reading from the causal reading
birch2014.note: not in Europe PMC (philosophy journal); Crossref metadata only.

birch2015.ref: Birch J, Okasha S (2015). Kin Selection and Its Critics. BioScience 65:22-32.
birch2015.note: Crossref dates the version of record 2014; the issue is 2015, vol 65 iss 1. Metadata only.

fisher1930.ref: Fisher RA (1930). The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
fisher1930.quotable: The genetical theory of natural selection
fisher1930.note: FOUNDATIONAL. A BOOK (Crossref monograph, Biodiversity Heritage Library scan DOI), not an indexed article.

price1972ftns.ref: Price GR (1972). Fisher's 'fundamental theorem' made clear. Annals of Human Genetics 36:129-140.
price1972ftns.note: the reinterpretation that rescued the theorem by restricting what it claims. Verified by direct DOI lookup, metadata only.

ewens1989.ref: Ewens WJ (1989). An interpretation and proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection. Theoretical Population Biology 36:167-180.
ewens1989.quotable: Fisher's "Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection" has long caused controversy in population genetics theory

ewens2015.ref: Ewens WJ, Lessard S (2015). On the interpretation and relevance of the Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection. Theoretical Population Biology 104:59-67.
ewens2015.quotable: Price's (1972) paper was the first to lead to an understanding of th
ewens2015.note: the quotable line is truncated exactly as the fetched abstract field returned it

basener2018.ref: Basener WF, Sanford JC (2018). The fundamental theorem of natural selection with mutations. Journal of Mathematical Biology 76:1589-1622.
basener2018.quotable: The mutation-selection process is the most fundamental mechanism of evolution
basener2018.side: claims the theorem fails once mutation is included
basener2018.note: the paper's own abstract misdates Fisher's proof to 1935 (it is 1930); that is the fetched text, not an error here.

hancock2024.ref: Hancock ZB, Cardinale DS (2024). Back to the fundamentals: a reply to Basener and Sanford 2018. Journal of Mathematical Biology 88:54.
hancock2024.quotable: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection has haunted theoretical population genetic literature since it was proposed in 1930
hancock2024.side: the direct critique of Basener & Sanford

grafen2018.ref: Grafen A (2018). The left hand side of the Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection. Journal of Theoretical Biology 456:175-189.
grafen2018.quotable: The fundamental theorem of natural selection is explained here in very simple terms, suitable for students
grafen2018.side: a third live position; Lessard & Ewens replied (PMID 30991074)

eigen1971.ref: Eigen M (1971). Selforganization of matter and the evolution of biological macromolecules. Naturwissenschaften 58:465-523.
eigen1971.quotable: Selforganization of matter and the evolution of biological macromolecules
eigen1971.note: FOUNDATIONAL, the error threshold and Eigen's paradox. No abstract in the record.

eigen1977.ref: Eigen M, Schuster P (1977). The hypercycle. A principle of natural self-organization. Part A: Emergence of the hypercycle. Naturwissenschaften 64:541-565.
eigen1977.quotable: The hypercycle. A principle of natural self-organization. Part A: Emergence of the hypercycle.
eigen1977.note: the hypercycle escape from the paradox. No abstract in the record.

takeuchi2007.ref: Takeuchi N, Hogeweg P (2007). Error-threshold exists in fitness landscapes with lethal mutants. BMC Evolutionary Biology 7:15.
takeuchi2007.quotable: One of the important insights of quasi-species theory is an error-threshold
takeuchi2007.note: whether the error threshold survives realistic landscapes; see also their 2005 phenotypic error-threshold paper, PMID 15691379

kleiber1932.ref: Kleiber M (1932). Body size and metabolism. Hilgardia 6:315-353.
kleiber1932.note: FOUNDATIONAL, Kleiber's law. Crossref metadata only. The 1947 review is also verified: Physiological Reviews 27:511-541, PMID 20267758.

west1997.ref: West GB, Brown JH, Enquist BJ (1997). A general model for the origin of allometric scaling laws in biology. Science 276:122-126.
west1997.quotable: Allometric scaling relations, including the 3/4 power law for metabolic rates, are characteristic of all organisms
west1997.side: derives 3/4 from a fractal network model

dodds2001.ref: Dodds PS, Rothman DH, Weitz JS (2001). Re-examination of the '3/4-law' of metabolism. Journal of Theoretical Biology 209:9-27.
dodds2001.quotable: Since simple dimensional analysis suggests alpha = 2/3, we consider this to be a null hyp
dodds2001.side: argues 2/3 is the null hypothesis and 3/4 is not established

kolokotrones2010.ref: Kolokotrones T, Savage V, Deeds EJ, Fontana W (2010). Curvature in metabolic scaling. Nature 464:753-756.
kolokotrones2010.quotable: For more than three-quarters of a century it has been assumed that basal metabolic rate increases as body mass raised to some power p
kolokotrones2010.side: no single exponent exists; the relation is curved
kolokotrones2010.note: the exchange continued: MacKay comment PMID 21335012, reply PMID 21497609

white2009.ref: White CR, Blackburn TM, Seymour RS (2009). Phylogenetically informed analysis of the allometry of mammalian basal metabolic rate supports neither geometric nor quarter-power scaling. Evolution 63:2658-2667.
white2009.quotable: The form of the relationship between the basal metabolic rate (BMR) and body mass (M) of mammals has been at issue for almost seven decades
white2009.note: mammals only; the avian analyses by the same authors were deliberately not used, because this project holds a clade out as a blind exam.

crick1968.ref: Crick FH (1968). The origin of the genetic code. Journal of Molecular Biology 38:367-379.
crick1968.quotable: The origin of the genetic code
crick1968.note: FOUNDATIONAL, the frozen-accident hypothesis. No abstract in the record.

koonin2009.ref: Koonin EV, Novozhilov AS (2009). Origin and evolution of the genetic code: the universal enigma. IUBMB Life 61:99-111.
koonin2009.quotable: The genetic code is nearly universal, and the arrangement of the codons in the standard codon table is highly nonrandom
koonin2009.note: modern synthesis of the competing theories

freeland1998.ref: Freeland SJ, Hurst LD (1998). The genetic code is one in a million. Journal of Molecular Evolution 47:238-248.
freeland1998.quotable: Statistical and biochemical studies of the genetic code have found evidence of nonrandom patterns in the distribution of codon assignments
freeland1998.note: the error-minimisation argument against pure frozen accident; follow-up PMID 10742043

medawar1952.ref: Medawar PB (1952). An Unsolved Problem of Biology. London: H.K. Lewis. Reprinted in The Uniqueness of the Individual, pp 44-70.
medawar1952.note: FOUNDATIONAL but a BOOK/lecture. Only the Routledge reprint chapter DOI could be fetched (Crossref issued year 2019); the 1952 original has no verifiable DOI.

williams1957.ref: Williams GC (1957). Pleiotropy, natural selection, and the evolution of senescence. Evolution 11:398-411.
williams1957.quotable: PLEIOTROPY, NATURAL SELECTION, AND THE EVOLUTION OF SENESCENCE
williams1957.note: FOUNDATIONAL, antagonistic pleiotropy. Not in Europe PMC; verified by direct DOI lookup. The record's title is in capitals.

kirkwood1977.ref: Kirkwood TB (1977). Evolution of ageing. Nature 270:301-304.
kirkwood1977.quotable: An evolutionary view of ageing suggests that mortality may be due to an energy-saving strategy of reduced error regulation in somatic cells

gems2013.ref: Gems D, Partridge L (2013). Genetics of longevity in model organisms: debates and paradigm shifts. Annual Review of Physiology 75:621-644.
gems2013.quotable: Discovering the biological basis of aging is one of the greatest remaining challenges for science

gems2022.ref: Gems D (2022). The hyperfunction theory: An emerging paradigm for the biology of aging. Ageing Research Reviews 74:101557.
gems2022.quotable: The process of senescence (aging) is predominantly determined by the action of wild-type genes

blagosklonny2021.ref: Blagosklonny MV (2021). The hyperfunction theory of aging: three common misconceptions. Oncoscience 8:103-107.
blagosklonny2021.quotable: The hyperfunction theory of aging: three common misconceptions

gems2013ros.ref: Gems D, de la Guardia Y (2013). Alternative Perspectives on Aging in Caenorhabditis elegans: Reactive Oxygen Species or Hyperfunction? Antioxidants & Redox Signaling 19:321-329.
gems2013ros.quotable: An influential theory has it that aging is the result of an accumulation of molecular damage, caused in particular by reactive oxygen species
gems2013ros.side: states the damage (ROS) account explicitly as the rival

wagner1996.ref: Wagner GP, Altenberg L (1996). Perspective: Complex adaptations and the evolution of evolvability. Evolution 50:967-976.
wagner1996.quotable: The problem of complex adaptations is studied in two largely disconnected research traditions: evolutionary biology and evolutionary computer science
wagner1996.note: FOUNDATIONAL. The Europe PMC title is in capitals in the record.

pigliucci2008.ref: Pigliucci M (2008). Is evolvability evolvable? Nature Reviews Genetics 9:75-82.
pigliucci2008.quotable: biologists have increasingly been asking whether the ability to evolve--the evolvability--of biological systems, itself evolves

payne2019.ref: Payne JL, Wagner A (2019). The causes of evolvability and their evolution. Nature Reviews Genetics 20:24-38.
payne2019.quotable: Evolvability is the ability of a biological system to produce phenotypic variation that is both heritable and adaptive

lassig2017.ref: Lassig M, Mustonen V, Walczak AM (2017). Predicting evolution. Nature Ecology & Evolution 1:77.
lassig2017.quotable: The face of evolutionary biology is changing: from reconstructing and analysing the past to predicting future evolutionary processes
lassig2017.note: the programmatic review of evolutionary prediction

devisser2014.ref: de Visser JA, Krug J (2014). Empirical fitness landscapes and the predictability of evolution. Nature Reviews Genetics 15:480-490.
devisser2014.quotable: The genotype-fitness map (that is, the fitness landscape) is a key determinant of evolution, yet it has mostly been used as a superficial metaphor

nosil2020.ref: Nosil P, Flaxman SM, Feder JL, Gompert Z (2020). Increasing our ability to predict contemporary evolution. Nature Communications 11:5592.
nosil2020.quotable: Increasing our ability to predict contemporary evolution
nosil2020.note: the Europe PMC record carries no abstract text.

hutchison2016.ref: Hutchison CA 3rd, Chuang RY, Noskov VN, Assad-Garcia N, Deerinck TJ, Ellisman MH, et al. (2016). Design and synthesis of a minimal bacterial genome. Science 351:aad6253.
hutchison2016.quotable: We used whole-genome design and complete chemical synthesis to minimize the 1079-kilobase pair synthetic genome of Mycoplasma mycoides JCVI-syn1.0

pelletier2021.ref: Pelletier JF, Sun L, Wise KS, Assad-Garcia N, Karas BJ, Deerinck TJ, et al. (2021). Genetic requirements for cell division in a genomically minimal cell. Cell 184:2430-2440.e16.
pelletier2021.quotable: Genomically minimal cells, such as JCVI-syn3.0, offer a platform to clarify genes underlying core physiological processes

breuer2019.ref: Breuer M, Earnest TM, Merryman C, Wise KS, Sun L, Lynott MR, et al. (2019). Essential metabolism for a minimal cell. eLife 8:e36842.
breuer2019.quotable: JCVI-syn3A, a robust minimal cell with a 543 kbp genome and 493 genes, provides a versatile platform to study the basics of life
breuer2019.note: the syn3A essential-metabolism reconstruction. Europe PMC renders the second author as 'Earnest EE'; the published form is Earnest TM.

thompson1917.ref: Thompson DW (1917). On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press.
thompson1917.note: FOUNDATIONAL and this repo's subject. A BOOK (Crossref monograph, Biodiversity Heritage Library scan DOI), not an indexed article.

umulis2013.ref: Umulis DM, Othmer HG (2013). Mechanisms of scaling in pattern formation. Development 140:4830-4843.
umulis2013.quotable: Many organisms and their constituent tissues and organs vary substantially in size but differ little in morphology
umulis2013.note: the modern framing of the scaling question

benzvi2010.ref: Ben-Zvi D, Barkai N (2010). Scaling of morphogen gradients by an expansion-repression integral feedback control. PNAS 107:6924-6929.
benzvi2010.quotable: Despite substantial size variations, proportions of the developing body plan are maintained with a remarkable precision
benzvi2010.note: FOUNDATIONAL expansion-repression mechanism; the Drosophila wing-disc test is PMID 21835621

cheung2011.ref: Cheung D, Miles C, Kreitman M, Ma J (2011). Scaling of the Bicoid morphogen gradient by a volume-dependent production rate. Development 138:2741-2749.
cheung2011.quotable: An important feature of development is the formation of patterns that are proportional to the overall size of the embryo
cheung2011.note: an alternative scaling mechanism to expansion-repression
